notes: Fictional subject and object (moved from 0001): a nonce noun ('wug' style) and its nonce plural in the real relation singular_of, with a goose-style plural. Determinate queries compare it with real nouns (Q1) and build a compound's plural on it (Q2), the one route in each. Q3 and Q4 ask closed lists of real nouns ('foot, goose, tooth'; 'goose' alone among '-oose' nouns) that the new noun joins. They were indeterminate (a world that kept the stored list said yes) until 2026-10-31; that world kept 'only these' beside a new member it calls different, so it was inconsistent (owl/FINDINGS.md A1), and both are now determinate 'no'. A model answering yes holds the insert only as a patch. Q3 leaves out compounds (forefoot, eyetooth); Q4 leaves out compounds of 'goose' (Canada goose, snow goose: plural in -geese) and says 'standard' plural because 'mongeese' and 'meese' are jocular (Wikipedia). Near query asks the real 'moose', so a leak ('meese' by analogy) is caught. Grammar ABox, and subject_object inserts, may have all derived queries determinate, so the record has no worlds.
